new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: The effect of ribavirin on the cell cycle of EGF-stimulated rat hepatocytes was analyzed by DNA content measurement in propidium iodide-stained cells using a flow cytometer. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In patients (about 9% of those with IBD) unable to achieve therapeutic erythrocyte 6-TGN concentrations, increased thiopurine doses fail to improve the active metabolite and hepatotoxic levels of erythrocyte 6-MMPR may develop due to the nonlinear kinetics of azathioprine metabolism. Among such patients with skewed thiopurine metabolism that favours methylation of metabolites, 24% develop dose-dependent hepatotoxicity, which is attributed to accumulation of the methylated metabolite 6-MMPR.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: assay_format=imaging_or_morphometry | biological_system_context=Cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (cryoheps, lot HC3-30), sandwich-cultured in Long-Term medium for 10 d from the next day after seeding and then in CDI maintenance medium (CM medium) for 5 d; intrinsically metabolically competent primary hepatocytes.
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_category=canalicular_morphology_or_dynamics | endpoint_metric=bile canalicular length and average canalicular area per image (anti-BSEP stained)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=bile canaliculi (CDFDFA fluorescence and anti-BSEP immunostaining) | exposure_conditions=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine (AMPK inhibitor) added during the 5 d culture on the CM medium; test concentration not reported in the extracted text. | extra_details=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine is described in the paper as an AMP inhibitor. Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). The paper did not report a numeric area/length value. The original article calls 2-prime,5-prime-dideoxyadenosine an AMPK inhibitor. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: The effect of ribavirin on the cell cycle of EGF-stimulated rat hepatocytes was analyzed by DNA content measurement in propidium iodide-stained cells using a flow cytometer. Stimulation with EGF gave a significant increase of the S-phase compartment at 72 h. In the presence of 50 µmol/L ribavirin, the G1-S transition of EGF-stimulated hepatocytes was significantly delayed: the number of cells in S phase was low at 72 h and significantly increased only at 96 h of culture.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In EGF-stimulated primary rat hepatocytes, the addition of ribavirin inhibited [3H]-thymidine uptake in a dose-dependent fashion. Exposure of EGF-treated rat hepatocytes for 3 days to 1 µmol/L and 50 µmol/L ribavirin resulted, respectively, in a significant decrease and a nearly complete suppression of DNA synthesis without appearance of morphological changes. [3H]-Thymidine incorporation was also effectively suppressed by mycophenolic acid at 10 µmol/L without any toxic effect.

MDR3 (Abcb4) is a canalicular phospholipid translocator under the SAM-PEMT-LRH-1 axis. DZA/homocysteine also reduced other LRH-1 target genes (Cyp8b1, Shp, Apoa1, Scarb1, Gls2); only the Mdr3 (named hepatobiliary transporter) result is extracted here. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To test the link between SAM and PEMT in LRH-1 target gene expression, the authors treated cells with 3-Deazaadenosine (DZA), a specific inhibitor of PEMT enzymatic activity, and with a high dose acute homocysteine treatment that disrupts SAM-to-SAH flow. Both DZA and acute homocysteine treatments decreased mRNA expression of Lrh-1 target genes including Cyp8b1 and Shp, and reduced LRH-1 Gal4-LBD luciferase reporter activity. Expression of several other LRH-1 target genes, including Apoa1, Scarb1, Gls2 and Mdr3, was also reduced upon DZA or homocysteine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=increased—ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 significantly induced, indicating restored hepatic differentiation; no ALB induction in Hep3B (already elevated ~7.5-fold in non-reconditioned Hep3B versus HepG2)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=2 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=reconditioning exposure to 2 uM 5-AZA for 12 days; total RNA extracted after 3 and 5 days of culture without 5-AZA (T1 and T2) | exposure_regimen=repeated_dose_with_recovery | extra_details=Phenotype named: restoration of hepatocyte differentiation markers (differentiated-function/reserve endpoint). new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To test the link between SAM and PEMT in LRH-1 target gene expression, the authors treated cells with 3-Deazaadenosine (DZA), a specific inhibitor of PEMT enzymatic activity, and with a high dose acute homocysteine treatment that disrupts SAM-to-SAH flow. Expression of several other LRH-1 target genes, including Apoa1, Scarb1, Gls2 and Mdr3, was also reduced upon DZA or homocysteine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Reverse transcriptase inhibitors inhibited MRP1 in vitro using CMF as the probe. With the exception of abacavir (no effect on MRP3), all the tested compounds increased intracellular CMF fluorescence in a concentration-dependent manner in cell lines overexpressing MRP2 or MRP3; emtricitabine exhibited the most pronounced inhibitory effect together with delavirdine and efavirenz.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Cryopreserved human hepatocytes; in-vitro assay used concurrently for CYP isoenzyme activity evaluation (CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4) and cell-associated uptake measurement | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=viability_or_cell_number | assay_and_readout=Cytotoxicity assessment in cryopreserved human hepatocytes—qualitative outcome
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule is mipomersen sodium (ISIS 301012), a 20-mer phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide targeting human apoB-100 mRNA. Cytotoxicity result is qualitative with no numeric potency, assay readout, exposure duration, or vehicle concentration reported in the provided text; the 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) top concentration and <10% CYP inhibition are reported for the enzyme-activity evaluation, which is a CYP assay without a concurrent hepatocyte health/reserve endpoint and is therefore not extracted as an eligible hepatocyte phenotype. No quantitative or regimen details for the cytotoxicity assessment were supplied in the text window. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the in-vitro evaluation in cryopreserved human hepatocytes, mipomersen sodium was tested and exhibited no cytotoxicity. The same in-vitro study showed significant cell uptake by analysing cell-associated concentrations of mipomersen sodium, and all evaluated CYP enzyme activities had <10% inhibition at tested concentrations up to 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) of mipomersen sodium.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: assay_format=imaging_or_morphometry | biological_system_context=Cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (cryoheps, lot HC3-30), sandwich-cultured in Long-Term medium for 10 d from the next day after seeding and then in CDI maintenance medium (CM medium) for 5 d; intrinsically metabolically competent primary hepatocytes.
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_category=canalicular_morphology_or_dynamics | endpoint_metric=bile canalicular length and average canalicular area per image (anti-BSEP stained)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=bile canaliculi (CDFDFA fluorescence and anti-BSEP immunostaining) | exposure_conditions=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine (AMPK inhibitor) added during the 5 d culture on the CM medium; test concentration not reported in the extracted text. | extra_details=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine is described in the paper as an AMP inhibitor. Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Two bile-acid-drug conjugates, BA-floxuridine and BA-ribavirin, were evaluated for liver-specific drug delivery. new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=increased—ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 significantly induced, indicating restored hepatic differentiation; no ALB induction in Hep3B (already elevated ~7.5-fold in non-reconditioned Hep3B versus HepG2)

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: CPA is reported to induce cholestasis but showed a low PC1 value in the current study. Stone et al. observed that plasma bile salt concentration was increased in rats after administration of 10 mg/kg of CPA, and suggested that CPA inhibits the uptake of bile acids from the portal blood into hepatocytes. No change in liver histology was seen in cholestasis caused by CPA, suggesting the intracellular bile-acid cytotoxicity is not severe.

Drug administered for 3 months. | extra_details=CPA rechallenge-like episode (second hepatotoxicity event) with worse clinical evolution requiring corticotherapy; dechallenge by discontinuation; most reported adverse hepatic reactions suggest drug-induced idiosyncratic mechanism with direct toxicity not excluded (direct hepatotoxicity from oxidative CYP metabolism producing electrophilic metabolites has been proposed experimentally); injury may progress to cirrhosis (refs 19,20). | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the reported case, the patient developed a second episode of hepatotoxicity with worse clinical evolution requiring corticotherapy after CPA therapy was started 4 months after the first episode, with normal bilirubin values at initiation. Liver biopsy showed an inflammatory infiltrate with lymphocytes, occasional eosinophils and regenerative nodules. It has been reported that liver injury associated with both flutamide and CPA may progress to cirrhosis; both drugs had been administered for 3 months, and the relative role of each in cirrhosis could not be ascertained.

Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). The paper did not report a numeric area/length value. The original article calls 2-prime,5-prime-dideoxyadenosine an AMPK inhibitor. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=other_hepatocyte_function_or_reserve | assay_and_readout=RT-qPCR—mRNA levels of hepatocyte differentiation markers ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 in reconditioned versus control HCC cells
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=increased—ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 significantly induced, indicating restored hepatic differentiation; no ALB induction in Hep3B (already elevated ~7.5-fold in non-reconditioned Hep3B versus HepG2)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=2 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=reconditioning exposure to 2 uM 5-AZA for 12 days; total RNA extracted after 3 and 5 days of culture without 5-AZA (T1 and T2) | exposure_regimen=repeated_dose_with_recovery | extra_details=Phenotype named: restoration of hepatocyte differentiation markers (differentiated-function/reserve endpoint). Non-reconditioned HCC cells were used as controls. CYP1A2, TAT, G6Pc, and HNF4A mRNAs also upregulated in reconditioned cells; CDH1 augmented; AFP downregulated. Exposure regimen classified as repeated_dose_with_recovery because cells were cultured without 5-AZA (3 and 5 days) before RNA assessment. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: CPA is reported to induce cholestasis but showed a low PC1 value in the current study. Stone et al. observed that plasma bile salt concentration was increased in rats after administration of 10 mg/kg of CPA, and suggested that CPA inhibits the uptake of bile acids from the portal blood into hepatocytes. No change in liver histology was seen in cholestasis caused by CPA, suggesting the intracellular bile-acid cytotoxicity is not severe.

Drug administered for 3 months. | extra_details=CPA rechallenge-like episode (second hepatotoxicity event) with worse clinical evolution requiring corticotherapy; dechallenge by discontinuation; most reported adverse hepatic reactions suggest drug-induced idiosyncratic mechanism with direct toxicity not excluded (direct hepatotoxicity from oxidative CYP metabolism producing electrophilic metabolites has been proposed experimentally); injury may progress to cirrhosis (refs 19,20). | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the reported case, the patient developed a second episode of hepatotoxicity with worse clinical evolution requiring corticotherapy after CPA therapy was started 4 months after the first episode, with normal bilirubin values at initiation. Liver biopsy showed an inflammatory infiltrate with lymphocytes, occasional eosinophils and regenerative nodules. It has been reported that liver injury associated with both flutamide and CPA may progress to cirrhosis; both drugs had been administered for 3 months, and the relative role of each in cirrhosis could not be ascertained.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=other_hepatocyte_function_or_reserve | assay_and_readout=RT-qPCR—mRNA levels of hepatocyte differentiation markers ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 in reconditioned versus control HCC cells
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=increased—ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 significantly induced, indicating restored hepatic differentiation; no ALB induction in Hep3B (already elevated ~7.5-fold in non-reconditioned Hep3B versus HepG2)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=2 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=reconditioning exposure to 2 uM 5-AZA for 12 days; total RNA extracted after 3 and 5 days of culture without 5-AZA (T1 and T2) | exposure_regimen=repeated_dose_with_recovery | extra_details=Phenotype named: restoration of hepatocyte differentiation markers (differentiated-function/reserve endpoint). Non-reconditioned HCC cells were used as controls. CYP1A2, TAT, G6Pc, and HNF4A mRNAs also upregulated in reconditioned cells; CDH1 augmented; AFP downregulated. Exposure regimen classified as repeated_dose_with_recovery because cells were cultured without 5-AZA (3 and 5 days) before RNA assessment. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=plasma bile salts | exposure_conditions=Single administration of 10 mg/kg CPA (route not stated); plasma sampled after dosing | extra_details=Secondary reporting of a cited prior experiment (Stone et al., reference 44). Result is qualitative ('increased'); actual plasma bile salt values not given in this window. The mechanism (inhibition of bile-acid uptake from portal blood into hepatocytes) is the cited authors' inference, not directly assayed here. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: CPA is reported to induce cholestasis but showed a low PC1 value in the current study. Stone et al. observed that plasma bile salt concentration was increased in rats after administration of 10 mg/kg of CPA, and suggested that CPA inhibits the uptake of bile acids from the portal blood into hepatocytes. No change in liver histology was seen in cholestasis caused by CPA, suggesting the intracellular bile-acid cytotoxicity is not severe.

Drug administered for 3 months. | extra_details=CPA rechallenge-like episode (second hepatotoxicity event) with worse clinical evolution requiring corticotherapy; dechallenge by discontinuation; most reported adverse hepatic reactions suggest drug-induced idiosyncratic mechanism with direct toxicity not excluded (direct hepatotoxicity from oxidative CYP metabolism producing electrophilic metabolites has been proposed experimentally); injury may progress to cirrhosis (refs 19,20). | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the reported case, the patient developed a second episode of hepatotoxicity with worse clinical evolution requiring corticotherapy after CPA therapy was started 4 months after the first episode, with normal bilirubin values at initiation. Liver biopsy showed an inflammatory infiltrate with lymphocytes, occasional eosinophils and regenerative nodules. It has been reported that liver injury associated with both flutamide and CPA may progress to cirrhosis; both drugs had been administered for 3 months, and the relative role of each in cirrhosis could not be ascertained.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: CPA is reported to induce cholestasis but showed a low PC1 value in the current study. Stone et al. observed that plasma bile salt concentration was increased in rats after administration of 10 mg/kg of CPA, and suggested that CPA inhibits the uptake of bile acids from the portal blood into hepatocytes. No change in liver histology was seen in cholestasis caused by CPA, suggesting the intracellular bile-acid cytotoxicity is not severe.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the reported case, the patient developed a second episode of hepatotoxicity with worse clinical evolution requiring corticotherapy after CPA therapy was started 4 months after the first episode, with normal bilirubin values at initiation. Liver biopsy showed an inflammatory infiltrate with lymphocytes, occasional eosinophils and regenerative nodules. It has been reported that liver injury associated with both flutamide and CPA may progress to cirrhosis; both drugs had been administered for 3 months, and the relative role of each in cirrhosis could not be ascertained.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: assay_format=imaging_or_morphometry | biological_system_context=Cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (cryoheps, lot HC3-30), sandwich-cultured in Long-Term medium for 10 d from the next day after seeding and then in CDI maintenance medium (CM medium) for 5 d; intrinsically metabolically competent primary hepatocytes.
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_category=canalicular_morphology_or_dynamics | endpoint_metric=bile canalicular length and average canalicular area per image (anti-BSEP stained)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=bile canaliculi (CDFDFA fluorescence and anti-BSEP immunostaining) | exposure_conditions=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine (AMPK inhibitor) added during the 5 d culture on the CM medium; test concentration not reported in the extracted text. | extra_details=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine is described in the paper as an AMP inhibitor. Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). The paper did not report a numeric area/length value. The original article calls 2-prime,5-prime-dideoxyadenosine an AMPK inhibitor. This is source terminology; the canalicular phenotype alone does not validate a direct or selective AMPK target mechanism. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Cryopreserved human hepatocytes; in-vitro assay used concurrently for CYP isoenzyme activity evaluation (CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4) and cell-associated uptake measurement | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=viability_or_cell_number | assay_and_readout=Cytotoxicity assessment in cryopreserved human hepatocytes—qualitative outcome
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule is mipomersen sodium (ISIS 301012), a 20-mer phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide targeting human apoB-100 mRNA. Cytotoxicity result is qualitative with no numeric potency, assay readout, exposure duration, or vehicle concentration reported in the provided text; the 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) top concentration and <10% CYP inhibition are reported for the enzyme-activity evaluation, which is a CYP assay without a concurrent hepatocyte health/reserve endpoint and is therefore not extracted as an eligible hepatocyte phenotype. No quantitative or regimen details for the cytotoxicity assessment were supplied in the text window. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the in-vitro evaluation in cryopreserved human hepatocytes, mipomersen sodium was tested and exhibited no cytotoxicity. The same in-vitro study showed significant cell uptake by analysing cell-associated concentrations of mipomersen sodium, and all evaluated CYP enzyme activities had <10% inhibition at tested concentrations up to 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) of mipomersen sodium.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: On day 6 sandwich-cultured hepatocytes, incubation for 24 hours in low-Ca²⁺ medium containing LKB1 or AMPK activators prevented canalicular disruption, with no fragmentation of occludin or loss of apical ABCB1 and canaliculi significantly longer than in low-Ca²⁺ treatment alone (P<0.001). Figure 7 legend specifies AICAR (500 µM) as one of the activators added for 24 hours.

Guanosine prevented this effect, decreasing the ROS levels from 155 ± 10% to 99 ± 7% (*p* < 0.01). The HO1 inhibitor ZnPP IX (10 µM) abolished the guanosine effect. Guanosine had no effect on the control condition.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=ROS production (DCF fluorescence)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: ROS levels (measured by DCFH oxidation) increased 55% after azide exposure. Guanosine prevented this effect, decreasing the ROS levels from 155 ± 10% to 99 ± 7% (*p* < 0.01). The HO1 inhibitor ZnPP IX (10 µM) abolished the guanosine effect. Guanosine had no effect on the control condition.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=cultured cortical astrocytic cells; in vitro OGD ischemia model | assay_and_platform=DCF fluorescence emission assay; fluorescence (fold increase from control)
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=ROS production (DCF fluorescence)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Cryopreserved human hepatocytes; in-vitro assay used concurrently for CYP isoenzyme activity evaluation (CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4) and cell-associated uptake measurement | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=viability_or_cell_number | assay_and_readout=Cytotoxicity assessment in cryopreserved human hepatocytes—qualitative outcome
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule is mipomersen sodium (ISIS 301012), a 20-mer phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide targeting human apoB-100 mRNA. Cytotoxicity result is qualitative with no numeric potency, assay readout, exposure duration, or vehicle concentration reported in the provided text; the 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) top concentration and <10% CYP inhibition are reported for the enzyme-activity evaluation, which is a CYP assay without a concurrent hepatocyte health/reserve endpoint and is therefore not extracted as an eligible hepatocyte phenotype. No quantitative or regimen details for the cytotoxicity assessment were supplied in the text window. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the in-vitro evaluation in cryopreserved human hepatocytes, mipomersen sodium was tested and exhibited no cytotoxicity. The same in-vitro study showed significant cell uptake by analysing cell-associated concentrations of mipomersen sodium, and all evaluated CYP enzyme activities had <10% inhibition at tested concentrations up to 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) of mipomersen sodium.

Figure 7 legend specifies AICAR (500 µM) as one of the activators added for 24 hours.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: immune_stimulus_regimen=IFN-γ/LPS | exposure_schedule=BMDMs co-treated with UDPG (dose series 0, 100, 200 μM) and IFN-γ/LPS for 24 or 36 h; sampling at 24/36 h | extra_details=Dose-response (100, 200 μM) reported collectively without dose-specific values; n=3 biologically independent experiments, mean±SEM, one-way ANOVA, **p<0.01, ****p<0.0001. new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: assay_format=imaging_or_morphometry | biological_system_context=Cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (cryoheps, lot HC3-30), sandwich-cultured in Long-Term medium for 10 d from the next day after seeding and then in CDI maintenance medium (CM medium) for 5 d; intrinsically metabolically competent primary hepatocytes.
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_category=canalicular_morphology_or_dynamics | endpoint_metric=bile canalicular length and average canalicular area per image (anti-BSEP stained)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=bile canaliculi (CDFDFA fluorescence and anti-BSEP immunostaining) | exposure_conditions=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine (AMPK inhibitor) added during the 5 d culture on the CM medium; test concentration not reported in the extracted text. | extra_details=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine is described in the paper as an AMP inhibitor. Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). The paper did not report a numeric area/length value. The original article calls 2-prime,5-prime-dideoxyadenosine an AMPK inhibitor. This is source terminology; the canalicular phenotype alone does not validate a direct or selective AMPK target mechanism. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=0.125-20 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=48 h exposure; cells treated the day after seeding, read at 48 h; MTT reagent (5 mg/ml) added for 4 h before reading | exposure_regimen=single_continuous | extra_details=Focal molecule VB6 (vitexin 6), paper label 'VB6'. Cells seeded at 3-5 x 10^3 in 100 µl medium per well and treated with compound the following day; cell survival expressed as absorbance relative to untreated controls; data mean±SEM from three independent experiments per cell line; this record is for the fitted HepG2 IC50 (one metric record, not per underlying dose). | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: All cell lines were cultured with 5% FBS and treated with varying amounts of VB6 (0.125–20 µmol/l) for 48 h. Cytotoxicity was evaluated using an MTT assay, and the IC50 values were determined through nonlinear regression analysis. For the HepG2 liver cancer cell line, the cytotoxicity IC50 was 12.37±0.79 µmol/l. Data (mean±SEM) were calculated from three independent experiments. VB6 is vitexin 6.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=total bile acids (TBA) | exposure_conditions=Gastrodin supplementation in BDL rats (dose/route not stated in this window); serum TBA measured after the treatment period versus BDL-alone control. | extra_details=This is an untargeted total bile acid homeostasis measurement; the paper interprets it as gastrodin may not influence bile acid synthesis or transportation but significantly increases serum TBA. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: The serum, urine, bile and liver tissue biochemistry analyses showed that although gastrodin had no effect on urine, bile or liver tissue levels of TBA after BDL, it significantly increased serum TBA by 42.1 percent in BDL-gastrodin treated rats compared to the BDL-alone group. The serum TBA values were 177.17 ± 56.31 µmol/L in BDL (n=7) versus 251.83 ± 52.04 µmol/L in BDL-gastrodin (n=7), p < 0.05.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Collagen sandwich-cultured non-dividing primary hepatocytes at day 6, low-Ca²⁺ medium challenge (Ca²⁺ depletion-induced junction fragmentation) | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunostaining for occludin and ABCB1 with confocal z-series imaging—mean canalicular length per cell and canalicular network branching/polarity
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=no fragmentation of occludin or loss of apical ABCB1; canaliculi significantly longer than low-Ca²⁺ alone, P<0.001
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=500 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=24 h incubation in low-Ca²⁺ medium containing AICAR, endpoint read at 24 h (day 6 culture) | exposure_regimen=single_continuous | extra_details=Focal molecule = AICA riboside (AICAR), an AMPK/LKB1 activator; protective/rescue role against low-Ca²⁺-mediated canalicular disruption. Combined result reported for the individually tested activators together (Fig. 7C). Species of hepatocytes not explicitly stated in the provided text. Original figure compares the activators in separate treatment conditions; AICAR is not a four-compound cocktail. Preserve the reported protective canalicular phenotype. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: On day 6 sandwich-cultured hepatocytes, incubation for 24 hours in low-Ca²⁺ medium containing LKB1 or AMPK activators prevented canalicular disruption, with no fragmentation of occludin or loss of apical ABCB1 and canaliculi significantly longer than in low-Ca²⁺ treatment alone (P<0.001). Figure 7 legend specifies AICAR (500 µM) as one of the activators added for 24 hours.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: assay_format=imaging_or_morphometry | biological_system_context=Cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (cryoheps, lot HC3-30), sandwich-cultured in Long-Term medium for 10 d from the next day after seeding and then in CDI maintenance medium (CM medium) for 5 d; intrinsically metabolically competent primary hepatocytes.
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_category=canalicular_morphology_or_dynamics | endpoint_metric=bile canalicular length and average canalicular area per image (anti-BSEP stained)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=bile canaliculi (CDFDFA fluorescence and anti-BSEP immunostaining) | exposure_conditions=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine (AMPK inhibitor) added during the 5 d culture on the CM medium; test concentration not reported in the extracted text. | extra_details=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine is described in the paper as an AMP inhibitor. Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). The paper did not report a numeric area/length value. The original article calls 2-prime,5-prime-dideoxyadenosine an AMPK inhibitor. This is source terminology; the canalicular phenotype alone does not validate a direct or selective AMPK target mechanism. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122).
